linkedin:
Remote hiring managers read applications on a screen, between meetings, often in a second language. Yours needs to be scannable.

Lead with the exact job title and where you saw it. Then one sentence on why your recent work fits. Save the life story for later.

Remote teams want proof you can work without someone watching. Mention a project you ran with written updates, a document you owned, or a time zone gap you handled.

Match their words. If they write "customer support", do not write "client care." Hiring software and tired humans look for the same words.

Keep the CV to one clean page. Most recent remote or freelance work first, with what you shipped.

Follow up once, politely, after a week. One clear note reads as professional; several reads as pressure.

Full guide: http://fixtures:8000/no-numbers-post.md
